summary: Rode 100.5 mi from South Lake Tahoe to Folsom, CA, starting with a climb and then an ~8,000 ft descent through a burned forest. Road construction holds, aggressive drivers on the descent, and a bonk from not eating enough made it a hard day; the team reunited for dinner in Folsom with family friends and former Spokes rider Rebecca Lizarde.
contacts: Nunu's family, South Lake Tahoe CA (Airbnb donated for the night)
Aarushi's family friends, Folsom CA (dinner hosts)
Rebecca Lizarde, former Spokes rider, Folsom CA (joined dinner)
planning_notes: Route out of South Lake Tahoe starts with an immediate climb; the descent into Folsom is about 8,000 ft and runs through a recently burned forest with active fire crews along the road.
Two separate one-way construction traffic holds on the climb out of Tahoe (excavators working on the mountainside) cost riders a lot of time; leave early or expect delays on this stretch.
Drivers on the descent toward Folsom were aggressive (yelling, honking, cars trying to push riders off the road); a support vehicle or a tighter group may help here.
Riders bonked on this 100-mile day after not eating enough; schedule food stops before the long descents and carry real food, not only sugary drinks.
Family-arranged lodging (Airbnbs and hotels from team families) was used repeatedly across CO, UT, NV and CA; ask families of team members about hosting on rest days.

summary: Rode 108.1 mi from Folsom to Benicia, CA, planned with about ten side quests but stretched to 18 hours. Headwinds and crosswinds across the Sacramento Valley, closed rest stops, dark and freezing riding, and a sushi and IKEA detour delayed the group, who reached their host at 3:20 AM.
slept_at: Gretchen and Anthony's home (host), Benicia CA
contacts: Rajeev, college batchmate of Aarushi's dad, Folsom CA (hosted and fed the whole team on short notice)
Makisu Sushi, Sacramento CA (restaurant run by a friend's uncle of Caroline; donated a team meal)
Gretchen and Anthony, Benicia CA (hosts who took the team in at about 3:20-4:10 AM)
planning_notes: Sacramento to Davis is a windy trail alongside the freeway with a strong headwind blowing from the Pacific; drafting behind a teammate helped.
Davis to Dixon runs through farm roads with right-angle turns; riders faced headwind or crosswind strong enough to blow them into the main road.
Rest stops near Davis and Dixon were closed by evening: a bakery, Costco and a thrift store on the route were all shut when riders arrived. Carry food for the late stretch instead of relying on them.
Davis art museum closed before the team finished lunch; check hours in advance.
Lucky's grocery around mile 77 was open late (about 10:30 PM) and worked as a late-night resupply stop.
After dusk it got freezing and windy, the coldest conditions of the trip; keep a warm layer on the bike, not only in the support van, since only one rider had a jacket.
Riders spread out 20 to 60 minutes apart and the van had to leave to support lead riders, leaving some unsupported for about 2 hours; keep the group together before dark.

Adding about ten side quests and ten rest stops to a 108-mile day pushed arrival to 3:20 AM with a wake-up under three hours later; do not stack side quests on century days and protect the sleep window.
Late-night Red Bull at a 7-11 left riders wired and unable to sleep; avoid caffeine late at night on long days.
Fire bingsu (shaved ice) shop in Davis, found from a prior blog, was a strong food stop.
